questions.prompt: Which statement about a cooking egg white is correct?

choices.text: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it.
The white sets while its protein chains stay folded in tight coils
Gentle heat unfolds the protein chains, which bond into a network that traps the water as the white sets.
The white turns opaque because air bubbles are beaten into it in the pan

questions.misconception: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it. In fact The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set. Gentle heat unfolds the folded protein chains in the egg white, the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it, and the white turns opaque and sets firm with its water still held in the network.

questions.prompt: Why is the white heated gently before it can set?

choices.text: To boil all the water out of the white
To give the folded protein chains energy to unfold into long loose chains
To fold the chains more tightly so the white firms up
To dissolve the protein chains in the water

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: gentle heat unfolds the folded chains, and only unfolded chains can bond into the network that sets the white.

questions.prompt: A student says the white sets because its water leaves as it cooks. Explain, in two sentences, what actually sets the white.
questions.answer: The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set. Gentle heat unfolds the folded protein chains in the egg white, the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it, and the white turns opaque and sets firm with its water still held in the network.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to follow the chains: unfolding and bonding set the white, while the water stays held in the network.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what the fully set white is like, and where its water is.
questions.answer: The fully set white is opaque and firm and holds its shape, with its water still trapped in the pockets of the protein network.
questions.explanation: Scene 4 shows the set white: opaque and firm out of the pan, its water still held inside the bonded network.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the denaturation stages in order?

choices.text: Folded chains in runny white, heat unfolds the chains, chains bond and trap water, white sets firm
Heat unfolds the chains, folded chains in runny white, white sets firm, chains bond and trap water
Chains bond and trap water, folded chains in runny white, white sets firm, heat unfolds the chains
White sets firm, chains bond and trap water, heat unfolds the chains, folded chains in runny white

questions.explanation: Scene 1 starts folded, scene 2 unfolds, scene 3 bonds and traps the water, and scene 4 is the set firm white.
